chunks: My father narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Musa b. Ja'far b. Wahb al-Baghdadi from Ali b. Ma'bad from Ali b. Sulayman al-Nawfali from Fitr b. Khalifa from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:
When this verse was revealed — 'And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins' [3:135]

Iblis climbed a mountain in Mecca called Thawr and screamed at the top of his voice to his demons, and they gathered to him. They said: 'O our master, why have you called us?' He said: 'This verse has been revealed, so who will address it?' A demon from the devils stood and said: 'I will address it through such-and-such.' He said: 'It is not for you.' Another stood and said the same, and he said: 'It is not for you.' Then the slinking whisperer said: 'I will address it.' He said: 'With what?' He said: 'I make promises and give them false hopes until they commit sin. When they commit sin, I make them forget to seek forgiveness.' He said: 'You are for it.' So he assigned him with this task until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الاستغفار: Istighfar — seeking forgiveness from Allah, the antidote to Satan's plot
key_terms.الوسواس الخناس: Al-Waswas al-Khannas — the slinking whisperer, Satan's agent who whispers evil and retreats
key_terms.عفريت: Ifrit — a powerful demon/devil in Islamic cosmology

ai.seo_question: How did Iblis react to the revelation of Quran 3:135 about repentance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the reaction of Iblis (Satan) to the revelation of Quran 3:135, which promises divine forgiveness for those who repent after sinning. Alarmed, Iblis gathered his demons on Mount Thawr in Mecca to devise a counter-strategy. While various demons offered solutions, it was al-Waswas al-Khannas (the slinking whisperer, referenced in Quran 114:4) who proposed the winning tactic: entice people into sin with false promises, then make them forget to seek forgiveness. Iblis assigned him this task permanently until the Day of Resurrection.
